display.purpose: The one page headline. 1.875rem, stepping to 2.25rem at sm.

code.purpose: The invite code, and only the invite code. Marker red at 0.36em tracking so six characters survive being read aloud across a room.

card-name.purpose: The name written on a card — the thing that occupies a slot. Never a label about the thing.

body.purpose: Sentences. Tabular figures inherited from body.

body-small.purpose: The line under a heading, an empty-state sentence, a correction's message.

slot-label.purpose: The board's own small caps and the system's workhorse: column heads, section headings, statuses, counts, slot numbers, rail links. Shipped as the slot-label utility.

field-label.purpose: An input's label. Differs from a section heading downward — same ink, lighter weight, tighter tracking — never by contrast.

stat.purpose: Figures that live in a column — the PIR column, a standings run, the clock, a box score. JetBrains Mono at 500, tabular, slightly tightened. Never prose, and never a name.

motion.name: card-lands
motion.purpose: A card landing in its slot: opacity 0 and translateY(-0.375rem) to rest. Plays only on the row that genuinely just arrived, keyed off the ?arrived=1 that the create and join actions set.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Guarded inside the card-lands utility itself, not at each call site, so a new caller cannot forget. The state change still lands; only the travel is dropped.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.purpose: Hover and focus colour changes on interactive elements. Not animation; permitted everywhere interactive.

motion.name: rule-advances
motion.purpose: The marker rule leaving the slot that was on the clock and drawing itself across the next one. Painted by a pseudo-element because a border cannot be scaled from one end, and from the right on a slot carrying data-reversed, because every even round of a snake draft is drafted right to left. Keyed on data-advanced, set by board-scroll.tsx only when this viewer was watching.

motion.name: pick-springs
motion.purpose: Phase 10's third and final animation event: the slot the marker just left, springing shut on the pick it has taken. The same state change as rule-advances seen from the other end, which is why it is not a fourth event. The overshoot is in the keyframes so the app keeps one curve; it is 4% because the board's 1px ruling IS the state language. Only a slot that FILLED (a rollback empties one), only one slot (an autodraft burst moves the marker three places), never on a first paint. Keyed on data-landed, guarded inside the rule.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The draft room only, since 10.9: the measure opens to 80rem and the room splits acting (pool) from watching (radar, board, console, chat). No other surface uses it, and there is no md or xl.

containers.name: wide
containers.purpose: Lineup, matchday, team, pool, trades, standings, recap and draft beside the sidebar.

contrastFloors.scope: text and position colours on the ground (stock)
meaningful non-text boundaries (rule, rail) on the ground
text and position colours on stock-panel

contrastFloors.floor: 3:1 (measured 3.15:1 — the panel is LIGHTER than the ground, so it is the binding surface, not the ground)

contrastFloors.scope: faint chalk on the live field
contrastFloors.floor: 4.5:1 (measured 4.61:1) — this pairing is what FIXES live-sunk's lightness; a lighter bay puts a muted pool row under the floor
none, deliberately — a background against a background, where the boundary carries the state

components.name: Lineup court

components.html: ...

components.name: Player pool browser
components.description: Searchable and filterable player list with visible position, club and availability.

components.name: Comparison drawer
components.description: Keyboard-accessible side drawer with stored game and fixture data. Missing values stay explicit.

components.name: Matchday status
components.description: Names provisional, final, stale and unavailable states, with the last official feed check.

narrative.northStar: A slate basketball arena for preparing a five, following a game, and reviewing the league.
narrative.overview: The approved 2026 arena interface keeps separate sidebar sections and a five-destination phone bar. Structure and typography stay quiet; cyan, emerald, crimson and gold each have a specific state job. See DESIGN.md current contract and ADR-0009.
keyCharacteristics: Slate canvas and framed panels with small control corners, no decorative glow or gradients.
A fixed-ratio half court with distinct centers, forwards and guards and five legal G/F/C formations.
Cyan for active state, emerald for gain, crimson for injury or loss, gold for captaincy and caution.
Sidebar sections remain distinct; phone tabs are Lineup, Players, Matchday, League and More.
Provisional matchday values display freshness and defer to final stored scores.

rules.name: Color has a job
rules.body: Always pair status color with text, numbers, or shapes. Position badges always print G, F, or C.

rules.name: One lineup state
rules.body: Court, grid, captain, substitutions and formation controls edit the same lineup. Recording remains an explicit server action.

rules.name: Live honesty
rules.body: Name scheduled, in-play, stale, unavailable, provisional and final states. Finished-game snapshots are authoritative.

rules.name: Small corners
rules.body: Use small control corners and circular player markers. Avoid decorative shadows, gradients, glows and nested cards.

dos: Keep 44px touch targets and visible keyboard focus.
Use a fixed-ratio court and test phone and desktop widths.
Label locally saved edits and missing comparison data explicitly.
donts: Do not introduce salary-cap credits, vice-captains or a trade cart.
Do not use E2025 as a selectable fantasy season.
Do not present an unverified live feed as final.
openQuestions: Enable LIVE_FETCH only after observing the official Boxscore change during an actual game.
